name: Boulder–Park Cleaver
itinerary: Day 1: Hike Boulder Ridge Trail and climb to high camp (~5,700 ft). Day 2: Cross the Park Glacier, climb the cleaver, and summit (10,781 ft), then descend to camp and out.
descent_text: Reverse the cleaver and Park Glacier terrain back to the 5,700 ft camp, downclimbing the class 3 step where the fixed line was left, then follow the Boulder Ridge Trail back to the trailhead; expect rockfall exposure near the 9,300 ft buttress on the way down as well as up.
beta: The route follows the Boulder Ridge Trail to its end, then climbs steep heather and a short class 3 rock step onto the ridge, reaching a high camp around 5,700 ft. From there it crosses onto the Park Glacier and ascends to the base of the cleaver (~6,800 ft), following the cleaver as the climbing steepens, becomes icy, and grows exposed to rockfall near crevasses, before joining the upper mountain near the Boulder Glacier's summit approach.

waypoints.name: Boulder Ridge Trailhead (Trail #605, FR-1131)
waypoints.directions: Drive Baker Lake Road to FR-1130, then follow FR-1131 to its end at the Boulder Ridge Trailhead, around 2,700 ft. Boulder Ridge Trail #605 starts from the road's end. This is the lowest trailhead on the mountain, which is why the climb adds up to about 8,000 ft of cumulative gain — the biggest of any Baker route.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Follow Boulder Ridge Trail #605 about 2 flat miles to the boggy clearing at the wilderness boundary, then the user path up steep heather and a Class 3 rock step to camp where the ridge meets snow. Rope up and cross the lower glacier northwest to the toe of the cleaver near 6,800 ft, follow the cleaver, mostly on its north side, to the large rock buttress near 9,300 ft, then take one of the finishes past the buttress onto the summit plateau and Grant Peak.
